title: Yard Diving Tender (YDT) Request for Information (RFI)
description: PURPOSE: Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maritime hereby issues a Request for Information (RFI) on behalf of the U.S. Navy and Foreign Military Sales, Boats, and Craft Program Office (PMS 300) to assess the availability of existing or in development craft designs applicable to the procurement of the attached requirements describing a Yard Diving Tender (YDT) craft. A prospective solicitation would seek to acquire two (2) YDTs to replace the YDTs currently in use with the Naval Diving and Salvage Training Center (NDSTC). This RFI will assist the Navy in finding qualified small business sources to build the required YDTs. Please note that only U.S.-built and U.S.-flagged vessels will be considered. The Navy intends to continue recapitalizing its aging fleet and procure YDTs beginning in Fiscal Year 2027. The overall objective of this Request for Information is to conduct and update market research to support preliminary planning for the acquisition of the YDT. The Navy plans to award a contract to one or more builders in FY27 for up to 2 crafts for delivery to the following: Panama City Beach, FL Description & MISSION PROFILE: The YDTs will be used by Naval Diving and Salvage Training Center (NDSTC), including Center for Explosive Ordnance Disposal & Diving (CENEODDIVE) to conduct training in underwater operations to locate, render safe and/or recover submerged objects and ordnance; harbor clearance/search; and expeditionary salvage operations. Through this RFI, the Navy aims to identify potential, commercial or developmental craft designs for the YDTs based on the following characteristics. Potential sources should have the personnel, facilities, technical capability and production capacity to produce up to two (2) YDTs. The Navy is particularly interested in existing, proven vessel designs that meet the following characteristics or that could be modified to meet the following characteristics while maintaining proven hull forms, propulsion systems and other major design features. Key YDT attributes and requirements: length: ?52m (170ft) Beam: ?10m (33ft) Draft: ?3.6m Air Draft: ?15m Cruise speed: ?15 knots (at full load in Sea State 4) Range: ?400 nautical miles at cruise speed Station Keeping: Dynamic Positioning class 2 (DP2) through Sea State 3, Beaufort Force 4 Sea State: Fully mission capable (including station keeping) up to Sea State 3, Beaufort Force 4 Fully mission capable (excluding station keeping) up to Sea State 4, Beaufort Force 5 Capable of restricted operations (transit at cruising speed) up to Sea State 5 Beaufort Force 6 Capable of surviving (maintaining course and heading) up to Sea State 6, Beaufort Force 7 Regulatory Bodies: American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) Marine Vessel Rules, U.S. Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Title 33 and 46, U.S. Navy Diving Manual Deck Area: ?180 square meters aft of deck house rated to carry payloads with concentrated local loads of up to 1500 kg/square meter Stability: ABS requirements for Intact and Damage Stability Personnel Capacity: ? 50 embarked persons Cranes: Aft deck crane ?4,500 kg at 15 ft past deck edge Spaces (minimum requirement) Diving storage space: below the aft deck approximately 20 ft in length and the full width of the craft at a minimum Pilot House: full 360 degree field of view, command, control and navigation suite Crews Quarters: galley, messing and seating for 8, berthing for 4 Diving locker: ? 20 square meters located on main deck Passenger Space: Seating area with working surface for ?42 persons for instruction and rest. Food storage and prep area and sufficient heads provided within or adjacent An additional 32 square meter enclosed compartment with access to the aft deck Responses & Submission of Information Interested parties are free to submit any information which may assist the Navy in its market research in response to this RFI. Responses to this RFI are limited to 10 pages and should include any relevant drawings, specifications, and/or sketches. The Government is not requesting a formal proposal at this time; however, please include as much of the technical data listed below as practical under the time constraints of this inquiry. As a reminder: please properly mark, clearly identify, and segregate any proprietary information included in your response. The following information is requested: Data and/or information on any vessel or vessel design in a similar size and capability range as that described in the draft specification. Data may be submitted on existing vessels, vessels that are conceptual or in design. If vessel is conceptual or in design, please provide level of maturity. A description of the company�s relevant experience. Past experience performing construction of boats of similar dimensions and characteristics highlighting: construction techniques; portions of work which intended to be performed by the prime contractor and portions of work to be subcontracted, including identification of likely design agent; any intended teaming arrangements; and familiarity with Government contract requirements and drawing development. Examples of successful Government or commercial contracts of similar scope of work. A description of the boat design identified by the Contractor that meets or comes close to meeting the above listed design requirements. If applicable, identify the number of vessels and the years they were delivered. Provide approximate pricing for: Candidate vessel Delivery to stated location Engineering Cost Provide location of company production facilities. Describe facility production capacity (e.g., estimate on total construction time for one (1) YDT; how many YDTs can be built per year), based on current and projected yard-wide workload. The Navy recommends contractors to provide information demonstrating their capability/capacity for production throughput. When describing throughput, please address capability/capacity of facilities and how they are suitable to handle the physical components of the boat, stowage of Government Furnished Equipment (GFE), and the current and projected utilization of workforce and trades required to complete the YDT. The Navy further requests information regarding the estimated maximum production throughput of the boats per year, including constraints from other contracted and projected workload for other project/programs. Additionally, the Navy requests for contractors to state the minimum YDT quantity that would need to be guaranteed to respond to the requirements of the potential solicitation. Interested parties may also submit additional information on the following areas of interest: Vessel principal characteristics and capabilities General arrangement drawings and renderings Design, construction, regulatory and classification standards employed Company production capabilities and recent, relevant, production history Contact information Note: Interested parties do not have to meet all requirements listed in this RFI to submit a response. All responses received will be reviewed by the Government. This RFI constitutes market research being performed under Part 10 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and is not an RFP. The responses shall contain unclassified information only. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS If your organization has the potential capacity to perform the above described efforts, please provide the following information on company letterhead: 1) Organization name, address, e-mail address, web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming (>20%) is anticipated to deliver technical and industrial capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/

title: Sole Source
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) in Fort Detrick, MD intends to negotiate on a Sole Source Basis with Rotunda Scientific Technologies LLC under 12.201-1, only one responsible source. This is a Presolicitation notice in accordance with RFO 5.101. Award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to Rotunda for a E1000 Bruker Magnettech ESR5000 Benchtop ESR/EPR Spectrometer System. This includes associated hardware, software, and installation. The Bruker ESR5000 unit is a unique deployable spectrometer that meets the need for rapid assessment of radiological dose in the field in support of the DoW Biodosimetry Network, a DHA-led program. It is the only deployable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance spectrometer with the capability to meet the needs of the Services. This allows the Services to characterize potential deployed forces level of radiobiological exposure and/or contamination for determining health status, driving treatment and saving lives. The rapid assessment of radiological dose using the deployable spectrometer to process biological samples supports the DHA combat health support mission. If not acquired, DoW would not be able to promptly assess radiological dose in a radiological/nuclear environment. title: Technical Data Package - CWU-86A/P, CWU-87A/P
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircrew Division requires highly specialized engineering, technical, and manufacturing support to update the Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) for the CWU-86/P and CWU-87/P Anti-Exposure Suits to the new CWU-86A/P and CWU-87A/P designations. This technical update will incorporate critical design changes identified and tested during windblast evaluations (specifically sleeve pocket modifications and localized seam tape reinforcement). The Government intends to procure Val/Ver CWU-86A/P and CWU-87A/P suits built strictly from the newly revised draft TDP for physical inspection and configuration audit. This requirement will be solicited as a sole source procurement to Switlik Parachute Company (CAGE Code: 78673) as a simplified acquisition. Switlik is a small business and is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the CWU-86/P and CWU-87/P flight suit platforms. Because these suits are critical, highly specialized life-support items worn by military aircrews in extreme environments, maintaining absolute continuity in manufacturing standards, dimensional tolerances, and material specifications are critical to flight safety. Switlik possesses the proprietary manufacturing setups, historical patterns, and baseline engineering design knowledge. Introducing a non-OEM source to manufacture these validation units would introduce unacceptable technical risk, as any alternative contractor would need to reverse-engineer Switlik�s proprietary assembly, stitching, and specialized seam-sealing techniques. The proposed contract action is for technical data and supplies for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i): Only one source reasonably available (e.g., unique/highly specialized capabilities, proprietary technology, exclusive manufacturer). THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. Interested parties, however, may identify their interest and capability by responding to the requirement with a capability statement. The Government will consider all information received prior to the closing date of this combined synopsis/solicitation. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. No phone inquiries will be entertained. Responses shall be made in writing via e-mail to the attention of Ms. Amy Wescott using the contact information provided in this synopsis. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact Switlik Parachute Company, LLC.

This requirement will be solicited as a sole source procurement to Switlik Parachute Company (CAGE Code: 78673) as a simplified acquisition. Switlik is a small business and is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the CWU-86/P and CWU-87/P flight suit platforms. Because these suits are critical, highly specialized life-support items worn by military aircrews in extreme environments, maintaining absolute continuity in manufacturing standards, dimensional tolerances, and material specifications are critical to flight safety. Switlik possesses the proprietary manufacturing setups, historical patterns, and baseline engineering design knowledge. Introducing a non-OEM source to manufacture these validation units would introduce unacceptable technical risk, as any alternative contractor would need to reverse-engineer Switlik�s proprietary assembly, stitching, and specialized seam-sealing techniques. The proposed contract action is for technical data and supplies for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i): Only one source reasonably available (e.g., unique/highly specialized capabilities, proprietary technology, exclusive manufacturer). The Government will consider all information received prior to the closing date of this combined synopsis/solicitation. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. No phone inquiries will be entertained. Responses shall be made in writing via e-mail to the attention of Ms. Amy Wescott using the contact information provided in this synopsis. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact Switlik Parachute Company, LLC.

title: NNMC - HPDP Wellness Program Coordination Services
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Indian Health Service � Shiprock Service Unit Health Promotion & Disease Prevention (HPDP) Wellness Program Coordination Services Northern Navajo Medical Center (NNMC), Shiprock, New Mexico The Indian Health Service (IHS), Shiprock Service Unit is issuing this Sources Sought Notice (SSN) to identify capable Indian-owned economic enterprises � large (IEE) or small (ISBEE) � that can provide professional wellness coordination and health promotion services in support of the Northern Navajo Medical Center (NNMC) Health Promotion and Disease Prevention (HPDP) program. Services include wellness facility access for referred IHS patients and community beneficiaries, community-based health promotion event support, mental health wellness initiative support, health education training, culturally appropriate nutrition and cooking programs, concussion management equipment training support, and crisis prevention and de-escalation training for school staff within the Shiprock Service Unit. Other capable firms are also invited to respond to this SSN. The Contracting Officer will consider responses for Buy Indian Act (25 U.S.C. 47) opportunities first, then for set aside programs under the Small Business Act (41 U.S.C. 3104). Background and Description of Requirement The Shiprock Service Unit of the Indian Health Service serves a large and geographically dispersed Navajo population across 20 outlying chapters. Access to health promotion and wellness activities is limited for residents of these communities. The IHS HPDP department is seeking a qualified contractor to deliver a comprehensive, community-based wellness program that: Provides IHS patients and community beneficiaries � who present with a written referral or written provider guidance from an NNMC-authorized provider � access to exercise equipment and aquatic wellness facilities at contractor-secured locations within 25 miles of NNMC Shiprock, New Mexico; Plans, coordinates, and executes no fewer than eight community HPDP promotional events per performance year; Supports mental health wellness initiatives in a non-clinical capacity; Provides health education training and supplies for students, parents, and community members; Delivers a structured, culturally grounded community wellness program engaging a minimum of 50 unduplicated youth participants per performance year; Develops and delivers a healthy living and cooking education program no fewer than twice per month, focused on heart-healthy and diabetes-friendly Native American cuisine; Supports Impact Concussion equipment training for local schools within the Shiprock Service Unit; Provides evidence-based crisis prevention and de-escalation training for school staff. All services shall be performed at contractor-secured or contractor-managed facilities located within 25 miles of NNMC Shiprock, New Mexico. The contractor is responsible for securing all necessary facility agreements, staffing, supplies, and equipment. This requirement does not involve physical therapy, medical diagnosis, clinical treatment, or any service requiring licensure as a healthcare provider. The contemplated contract is a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract with a base year and three one-year option periods (four years total). NAICS Code and Size Standard The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this requirement is 624190 � Other Individual and Family Services, with a small business size standard of $12,000,000 in average annual receipts. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION Information collected from this notice is purely for market research purposes only and will be used to determine the contracting office's acquisition strategy, including competition, set-asides, and the identification of Indian-owned economic enterprises. Submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary. The government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred in responding to this request for information. description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS AND COMMERCIAL SERVICES General Information Document Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Solicitation Number: 9531BM26Q0029 Product or Service Code: 6640 � Laboratory Equipment and Supplies Set Aside: 100% Small Business Set-Aside NAICS Code: 333517 � Machine Tool Manufacturing Small Business Size Standard: 500 employees Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price (FPP) Purchase Order FOB Point: Destination Quotation Due Date: September 24, 2026, 4:00 p.m., Eastern Daylight Time (EDT) Contracting Office Address: National Transportation Safety Board Acquisition Division (CFO-30) 490 L�Enfant Plaza, SW Washington, DC 20594 Combined Synopsis/Solicitation This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The solicitation number for this requirement is 9531BM26Q0029. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Quotations (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01. The requirement is issued as a 100% total small business set-aside. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is NAICS code is 334516, �Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing�. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) requires the purchase and delivery of one (1) pulsed laser cleaning machine, SFX Laser BPC-500, or equal. The named product establishes the characteristics and level of quality that will satisfy the Government�s requirement. Equal products will be considered in accordance with FAR 52.211-6, Brand Name or Equal. The equipment shall be new and current production. Used, refurbished, remanufactured, demonstration, or protype equipment will not be accepted. Background The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is an independent Federal agency charged by Congress with investigating every civil aviation accident in the United States and significant accidents in the other modes of transportation -- railroad, transit, highway, marine, pipeline, and commercial space-- and issuing safety recommendations aimed at preventing future accidents. The NTSB has a requirement to purchase one (1) pulsed laser cleaning machine. This equipment will aid in the removal of rust, contaminants, coatings, and paint from portions of accident wreckage and components so that examination and testing can be performed. This type of evidence surface preparation has traditionally been done by contracting a third-party vendor for sandblasting. Laser cleaning is less damaging to the underlying material than abrasive sandblasting or chemical methods of surface contaminant removal and will better preserve the condition and features of the evidence under examination. Laser cleaning will also reduce the amount of hazardous material waste generated by sandblasting and chemical methods of surface preparation. Products The contractor shall provide firm-fixed pricing for the item listed below. The quotation shall include all costs necessary to provide the required equipment, operation manuals, one-year warranty, and FOB Destination delivery in accordance with this RFQ. CLIN 001: Description: Pulsed Laser Cleaner, Qty:1, Unit: EA, Unit Price: $_______, Extended Price: $_______ TOTAL QUOTED PRICE: $__________ Minimum Salient Characteristics The pulsed laser cleaning machine, shall meet the following minimum specifications: The laser cleaner shall be of the pulsed laser variety. The laser cleaner shall be capable of operating on 208V single phase power. The laser cleaner shall have a minimum of 500W output power. The laser cleaner shall have adjustable pulse width and frequency. The laser cleaner shall have multiple cleaning mode patterns. The laser cleaner shall have anti-reflection protection. The laser cleaner shall have a sturdy chassis with storage for the cables and laser head. The laser cleaner be furnished with Operation Manuals. The laser cleaner shall have a warranty against defects in materials and workmanship for a period of one (1) year from delivery date. The quotation shall clearly identify the manufacturer and exact model offered and shall include manufacturer technical literature sufficient to verify compliance with each minimum salient characteristic. Review the attached RFQ document and attachments which are attached hereto and incorporated herein for a detailed description of the requirement. Brand Name or Equal FAR 52.211-6, Brand Name or Equal, applies to this acquisition. A quoter offering the referenced SFX Laser BPC-500 shall identify the manufacturer and exact model offered. A quoter offering an equal product shall clearly identify the manufacturer and model number and furnish descriptive literature sufficient to establish that the proposed product meets or exceeds each minimum salient characteristic. For an equal product, the quotation shall include a concise compliance cross-reference identifying each salient characteristic, the offered specification, and the technical-literature page or section supporting compliance. Any modification required to make the offered product conform to the requirements shall be clearly identified. The Government will evaluate an equal product based on information furnished with the quotation or specifically identified in the quotation and reasonably available to the Contracting Officer. The Government is not responsible for locating technical information that the quoter has not identified. Delivery The offeror shall deliver the laser cleaner and all necessary operational manuals within 60 calendar days of the date of award. The equipment is to be delivered FOB Destination to: National Transportation Safety Board Office of Research and Engineering 401 Prince Georges Blvd Upper Marlboro, MD 20774 Basis for Award The Government intends to award one (1) firm-fixed-price contract to the responsible Contractor whose quotation conforms to the requirements of this RFQ and represents the lowest-priced technically acceptable quotation. The Government will evaluate quotations using the following factors: Technical Acceptability Price Factor 1: Technical Acceptability Technical Acceptability will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. To be determined technically acceptable, the quotation must offer a new pulsed laser cleaner that meets each minimum salient characteristic and other material requirement of this RFQ; provide sufficient technical information to verify compliance; meet the required delivery schedule; and take no exception to a material requirement. A quotation that does not demonstrate compliance with each minimum salient characteristic and other material requirement will be determined technically unacceptable and will not be considered for award. Features or capabilities exceeding the stated minimum requirements will not receive additional evaluation credit. Factor 2: Price The Government will evaluate the total firm-fixed price for the requirement and will evaluate price for reasonableness using appropriate price analysis techniques. Evaluation Factor Order of Importance Technical Acceptability is a threshold requirement. Among quotations determined technically acceptable, award will be made to the responsible quoter submitting the lowest total evaluated price. No tradeoffs will be made between price and non-price factors. Clauses and Provisions Please review and complete Attachment 1 and Clauses and Provisions, where applicable. The attachment is included hereto and incorporated herein for additional information.. title: Total Aircraft Wash System at 186th ARW
description: The Mississippi Air National Guard (MSANG), 186 Air Refueling Wing (ARW) is issuing this pre-solicitation notice to inform industry of an upcoming requirement for a Total Aircraft Wash System. This procurement will be conducted in accordance with the procedures outlined in RFO 12.201-1(c)(2). Please be advised that this notice is published solely to inform industry of the Government�s intent to solicit quotations directly from at least three total aircraft wash system manufacturers and suppliers. The Government does not intend to post a formal solicitation notice on SAM.gov. In accordance with RFO 12.201-1(c)(2), for acquisitions at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT), the Contracting Officer is electing to solicit quotations directly from suppliers. By posting this pre-solicitation notice, the Government is fulfilling the requirement to post a pre-solicitation notice in the GPE according to subpart 5.1. Award Timeline The targeted date for contract award is 30 September, 2026. Disclaimer This is a pre-solicitation notice only and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). Responding to this notice does not guarantee inclusion. The contracting officer will evaluate potential offers to evaluate their potential to be a responsible source before being solicited directly. For this notice, a responsible source will be a company whose primary industry is the manufacture or sale of total aircraft wash systems, has a satisfactory past performance, and is a small business. No formal solicitation document will be posted to SAM.gov for this requirement. It is the governments intent to solicit quotations directly from suppliers, however interested vendors may submit their company information for this requirement.

description: Lapin hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia mammografiatutkimuspalveluista lausuntoineen Lapin hyvinvointialueen ja Työterveys Lappica Oy:n tarpeisiin. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen (2) osa-alueeseen, joista tarjoaja voi jättää tarjouksen joko yhteen tai molempiin: 1. Mammografiatutkimuspalvelut lausuntoineen Rovaniemellä: Palvelu tuotetaan Palveluntuottajan toimitiloissa Rovaniemellä. 2. Mammografiatutkimuspalvelut lausuntoineen Kemijärvellä: Palvelu tuotetaan Tilaajan toimitiloissa Kemijärvellä Tilaajan laitteilla. Kummallekin osa-alueelle valitaan yksi (1) Palveluntuottaja. Palveluntuottajan tulee sitoutua tuottamaan palvelu kokonaisuudessaan tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Hankittavien palvelujen tarkempi sisältö ja sitä koskevat ehdottomat vaatimukset on kuvattu liitteessä 1 Palvelukuvaus ja ehdottomat vaatimukset. title: Consolidated Product-Line Management, Sustainment, and Modernization (CPMSM)
description: 1. Purpose The purpose of this notice is to obtain information and industry comments in anticipation of a future competitive requirement for the Consolidated Product-Line Management, Sustainment, and Modernization (CPMSM) program, which will continue supporting the objectives of the Consolidated Product-Line Management Plus (CPM Plus) program, focusing on the requirements, development, execution, management, and synchronization of the Live Training Transformation (LT2) Product-Line (P/L). With 23 LT2 products fielded to over 200 sites globally, the LT2 P/L successfully employs technical and acquisition strategies that significantly reduce fielding time, minimize acquisition costs, enable total ownership cost reductions, and enhance training benefits afforded to the warfighter. The incumbent contractor for the existing CPM Plus effort under contract number W900KK-20-D-0007 is General Dynamics Mission Systems, Inc., 12001 Research Parkway Ste 500, Orlando, FL 32826-3249. 2. Program Description The planned CPMSM contract vehicle will encompass the continued management of the evolution of the LT2 P/L and provide total life cycle support to those programs that utilize the LT2 P/L. It will continue to meet the requirements for a consolidated streamlined approach that: 1) Protects and leverages the Army's LT2 P/L investment. 2) Continues the development and evolution of the LT2 products/systems, core assets, architectural frameworks, and the LT2 P/L Construct. 3) Continues to provide efficient, effective, and agile methods to deliver military training products. Under the CPMSM program the Army will execute control of a system's life cycle within a System-of-Systems (SoS) environment to maximize the commonality, reuse and interoperability of the system, while maintaining integrity of the product lines from which it is based. CPMSM will continue to evolve the deliberate processes for managing the development, production, and sustainment of LT2 products. CPMSM will enable using organizations to maintain visibility and control of the configuration of those systems, and SoS integration for which they are responsible throughout the total system life cycle. The anticipated nature and complexity of the LT2 P/L work tasks (ranging from P/L architectural development, system development, SoS management to P/L core asset variability, and configuration management) associated with CPMSM requires mature and established processes, and therefore at least a Level 3 Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) company rating. 3. Request For Information The Government is conducting market research with companies that are interested in this requirement and/or portions therein. Specifically, the Government requests that companies address their capabilities and relevant experience as we inform our contracting strategy for CPMSM. The Government would also like to solicit feedback from industry on the recommended contracting strategy for the CPMSM effort. 4. Company Profile To assist the Government in determining if this can be set aside for small businesses, please provide the following administrative information: � Company Name, CAGE Code, and UEI Number. � Point of Contact (Name, Phone, Email). � Business Size Standard and Socio-Economic Status (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) under NAICS Code: 541512 for Computer Systems Design or 541511 for Custom Computer Programming). All strategies should strive to protect and leverage the Army's LT2 P/L investment, while evolving core assets and the LT2 Construct tools and processes to ensure technology relevance across the P/L. A web-based portal hosts a reference library and contains a multitude of information related to LT2 and CPM efforts. The library is located at https://lt2portal.mil. If you do not already have a LT2 Portal account then please go to the site and register for an account (click on register on top right hand side of the LT2 Portal home page, then fill in the information requested. 5. Submission Instructions The Government is exploring a range of acquisition strategies and plans to utilize the information gained from this White Paper to help further shape the acquisition strategy. Responses should be limited to a three (3) page max white paper, not including cover page, cover letter, table of contents and any other documentation submitted in response to Past Performance. Any proprietary concepts of information should be clearly identified as such. Submitted data and information will not be returned. Any information submitted in response to this RFI Notice is strictly voluntary. This notice is for information and planning purposes. The Government will not pay or otherwise reimburse respondents for information submitted. Industry is encouraged to suggest alternative NAICS codes that may better align with the requirements. Disclaimer: This notice does not constitute an invitation for bids or a request for proposal and is not a commitment by the U.S. Government to procure subject products or services nor will the Government reimburse any parties for costs associated with this request. The Government will use the information received to forge its acquisition strategy. Additionally, all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. No basis for a claim against the Government shall arise as a result from a response to this RFI. All correspondence and questions regarding this notice shall be directed to the Contracting Office POC and Program Office POC listed below: POINT OF CONTACT INFORMATION: Contracts POC: Reuel Dunn: reuel.p.dunn.civ@army.mil, 520-714-5529 Program POC: Courtney Flugstad: courtney.s.flugstad.civ@army.mil, 520-692-4037

description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) Aerial Targets Program Office (PMA-208), Patuxent River, Maryland, intends to enter into sole source negotiations and subsequently award a standalone �C-type� contract containing Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs) to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation (NGSC), San Diego, CA. The anticipated effort provides for the advance procurement of long-lead items in support of the BQM-34S Subsonic Aerial Target (SSAT), including but not limited to Enhanced Integrated Avionics Units (EIAU) and Brushless Aileron Actuators. The BQM-34S SSAT is a recoverable, subsonic aerial target system utilized for weapon systems test and evaluation and Fleet training. Contract award is projected for the second quarter of Fiscal Year (FY) 2028, with an anticipated period of performance of 24 months. This requirement will be procured under the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. NGSC is the sole designer, developer and manufacturer of the BQM-34S SSAT. NGSC is the only known source possessing the requisite knowledge, maintenance and repair experience, and noncommercial technical data and software rights to meet the Government�s requirements for the BQM-34S SSAT System. description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. THIS NOTICE IS ISSUED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR INVITATION FOR OFFERORS TO SUBMIT PROPOSALS. A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION WILL BE POSTED AT A LATER DATE WHICH WILL PROVIDE INSTRUCTIONS FOR OFFERORS TO RESPOND TO THIS OPPORTUNITY. Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF) is conducting market research to determine industry capability and interest in providing One (1) each 100kW Diesel Generator (DG) to serve as part of an emergency power supply system (EPSS) for providing primary power and/or standby backup power. title: Request For Information (RFI) Urgent Repair of the C-5 Moving Island Actuators
description: Request for Information 409 SCMS/GUMA Mechanical Section for Supply Chain Management Squadron Air Force Sustainment Center Robins AFB, GA FOR C-5 Moving Island Actuators Emergency Repair CAUTION: This market survey is being conducted to identify potential sources that may possess the expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet the requirements for qualification and repair of the C-5 Moving Island Actuators for use by United States Air Force (USAF) personnel. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation in this survey may not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards. The government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey. INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Below is a document containing a description of the C-5 Moving Island Actuators requirement and a Contractor Capability Survey, which allows you to provide your company�s capability. 2. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company�s capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capability to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) -Identify any areas of work that your company believes should be broken out exclusively for Small Business 3. Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. 4. Questions relative to this market survey should be addressed to Paige Mosley: paige.mosley.1@us.af.mil PURPOSE/DESCRIPTION: The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the repair data, expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements for the C-5 Moving Island Actuators NSN(s): 1680-01-185-7485, 1680-01-522-2388, 1680-01-179-8076, 1680-01-521-8824, 1680-01-181-5670, 1680-01-521-8823, 1680-01-180-0262, 1680-01-521-8826 for the USAF. The moving island actuators are part of the secondary flight control system that controls the moving island section of the slats. The moving islands provide aerodynamic sealing when the slats are retracted, and the moving island actuators move the moving islands out of the way when the slats are extended. These parts listed in the report are critical to the function of the slat system of the C-5 family of aircraft. Special tooling is required for the repair and overhaul of the moving island actuators called out in the overhaul manual. Companies are encouraged to provide responses to this questionnaire but are advised that their participation is voluntary and no reimbursement of any kind will be provided. Please see the attachment included.

description: Die Gemeinde Dümmer beabsichtigt aufgrund demografischer Veränderungen und bestehender baulicher und brandschutztechnischer Mängel den Umbau und die Sanierung der bestehenden Kindertagesstätte „Seepferdchen“. title: Udbud af Sundmolen Øst - Byggemodning
description: Udviklingsselskabet By & Havn I/S’ (i det følgende benævnt ”Ordregiver”) udbyder byggemodning af Sundmolen Øst, herunder udførelse af infrastruktur, en bro, tre byrum, inkl. et grønt byrum på Sundmolen Vest, samt forsyningsledninger og pumpestation for HOFOR. Entreprisekontrakten vedrører udførelsen af byggemodning på Sundmolen Øst samt udførelse af et grønt byrum på Sundmolen Vest i hovedentreprise (”Opgaven”). Derudover vedrører entreprisekontrakten delvis projektering som beskrevet i kontraktens pkt. 6. Opgaven består i hovedtræk af udførelse af forsyningsledninger for HOFOR, infrastruktur, bro og beplantning. Derudover omfatter opgaven projektering og etablering af en pumpestation. Den udbudte kontrakt forventes udført i tidsrummet november 2026 til juni 2028. For en nærmere beskrivelse af kontrakten og den udbudte opgave henviser Ordregiver til det samlede udbudsmateriale angivet i udbudsbetingelsernes afsnit 2. Ordregiver har valgt ikke at opdele opgaven i delkontrakter, idet det af hensyn til Ordregivers administration og for at minimere grænsefladeproblematikken er mest hensigtsmæssigt, at størstedelen af opgaven udføres af én og samme entreprenør.

title: Germany – Engineering design services for mechanical and electrical installations for buildings – MPI für Geoanthropologie, Jena - Umbau und Generalsanierung zum Institutsgebäude von zwei denkmalgeschützten Klinikgebäuden - Fachplanung Technische Ausrüstung (ELT)
description: Der Leistungsumfang betrifft die umfangreiche Generalsanierung von zwei denkmalgeschützten Bestandsgebäuden (ehemalige Kliniken) mit Planung und Umbau zu neuen Verwaltungs- und Laborräumen für das Max-Planck-Institut für Geoanthropologie in Jena. Auf dem Flurstück 105 / Lessingstraße 1 befindet sich die ehemalige Urologie mit einem denkmalgeschützten Teil aus dem Jahr 1914 und einem Anbau aus dem Jahr 1991. Auf dem Flurstück 102/5 / Lessingstraße 2 befindet sich die ehemalige HNO aus dem Baujahr 1928. Die Gebäude sind jeweils 4-geschossig mit zusätzlichem teilbelichtetem Kellergeschoss sowie nicht ausgebautem Giebelgeschoss. Gebäude und Gartenanlage stehen unter Denkmalschutz; daher ist eine enge Abstimmung mit dem Landesamt für Denkmalpflege bzw. der unteren Denkmalschutzbehörde erforderlich. Das Institutsgebäude wird überwiegend aus Büroflächen und Büronebenflächen bestehen. Weiterhin sind Seminarräume, ein Laborbereich mit Lagerflächen, Serverräume und ein Decision Theatre vorgesehen. Der Laborbereich wird als gemeinsam genutzter Laborpool für alle experimentell arbeitenden Organisationseinheiten ausgebildet. Der hochinstallierte Experimentalbereich mit Laboren, Laborlagern und Servern soll im Anbau der ehemaligen Urologie untergebracht werden. Die niedrig installierten Büro- und Kommunikationsflächen werden im denkmalgeschützten Teil der Urologie sowie in der HNO untergebracht. Gegenstand dieses VgV-Vergabeverfahrens sind die Leistungen der Fachplanung Technische Ausrüstung (ELT) gemäß § 55 HOAI in Verbindung mit Anlage 15 zur HOAI 2021 für die Anlagengruppen 4, 5 und 6 in den Leistungsphasen 2, 3 und 5 bis 9 sowie die im Vertrag und in dessen Anlage A beschriebenen Besonderen Leistungen. Das Projekt wird als BIM-Projekt im Open-BIM-Verfahren durchgeführt. Bestandteil des Auftrags sind außerdem die in den Vertragsunterlagen einschließlich Leistungsbild beschriebenen BIM-bezogenen Leistungen, Koordinationsleistungen sowie die Erstellung, Fortschreibung und Bereitstellung der Fachmodelle nach den vertraglichen Vorgaben. Weitere Angaben zur Ausgangssituation, Aufgabenstellung und zum Leistungsumfang ergeben sich aus Anlage 01 sowie aus dem Ingenieurvertrag Technische Gebäudeausstattung ELT einschließlich Leistungsbild. Besonderer Hinweis betr. Bieterfragen aufgrund besonderer äußerer Ereignisse (z.B. Sars-COV-2 oder Ukraine Krieg): Bitte berücksichtigen Sie bei Ihrer Angebotserstellung etwaige mögliche bzw. erkennbare Beeinträchtigungen, z.B. in Bezug auf die Verfügbarkeit von Materialien und Produkten, Arbeitskräften, eine evtl. verzögerte Beibringung von geforderten Nachweisen, Auswirkungen auf etwaige Nachunternehmer etc. Fragen, die in diesem Zusammenhang auftreten, bitten wir rechtzeitig vor Angebotsfrist über das Nachrichtensystem der eVergabe zu stellen.

Bauabschnitts im Plangebiet und auf externe Flächen, die im direkten Umfeld des Plangebietes liegen. description: Die Marienbad GmbH beabsichtigt die umfassende Sanierung und Modernisierung des Freizeitbades "MarienBad" in Bad Marienberg. Gegenstand der vorliegenden Ausschreibung sind Planungsleistungen der Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume gemäß § 34 HOAI in Verbindung mit Anlage 10 HOAI, beginnend mit der Leistungsphase 5. Die Planungsleistungen sollen die Leistungsphasen 5 bis 9 umfassen. Der Auftragnehmer übernimmt die vorliegenden Planungsunterlagen, prüft diese auf Plausibilität, Vollständigkeit, Widerspruchsfreiheit und Ausführbarkeit und entwickelt sie zur ausführungsreifen Planung fort. Die vorliegenden Unterlagen sind als Anlagen Bestandteil der Aufgabenstellung. In der Verbandsgemeinde Bad Marienberg (Rheinland-Pfalz/Westerwaldkreis) wird nur ein einziges Hallenbad für rund 20.000 Einwohner bereitgehalten. Das MarienBad als Erlebnisbad (Aktiv- und Bewegungsbad, mit Sauna und Wellnessbereich sowie Gastronomie und Wohnmobilpark) wurde am 04.11.1995 in Betrieb genommen. Das Gebäude befindet sich in der Bismarckstraße 65, 56470 Bad Marienberg, Gemarkung Langenbach bei Bad Marienberg, Flur 22, Flurstück 29/3. Die Hauptnutzung als Hallenbad mit Saunalandschaft bleibt erhalten. Nach einer Betriebszeit von knapp 30 Jahren ist eine grundlegende energetische Sanierung erforderlich. Dies betrifft insbesondere die technische Gebäudeausrüstung, die Badtechnik, die Gebäudehülle sowie wesentliche Innenbereiche. Die Maßnahme dient zugleich der Verbesserung der Betriebsabläufe, der Steigerung der Attraktivität und der Herstellung beziehungsweise Optimierung der Barrierefreiheit. Das MarienBad soll als barrierefreies Hallenbad für Menschen aller Altersgruppen, für Menschen mit und ohne Behinderung sowie für Menschen unterschiedlicher kultureller Herkunft ein Ort der Begegnung sein. Die Infrastruktur für Rollstuhlfahrer wird im Zuge der Planungsarbeit geprüft und, in Abstimmung mit dem Behindertenbeauftragten des Kreises, weitergehend optimiert.
